invariants.finding: D3 defines a reusable limiter/mass contract for the common kernel, not a separate SWAP variant.
No parsing, files, units or paths occur in the limiter contract.
Storage state, exchange results, supply capacity/control, accepted fluxes and scratch are explicitly separated.
D3 introduces no new persistent state; SWST remains D1-owned conserved state.
QDRATIO and projected-storage temporaries are scratch/trial results.
The limiter is scalar/batched arithmetic compatible with SoA MultiSWAP layouts.
Limiter outputs are trial-only; rejected trials cannot alter SWST or the accepted mass ledger.
The same committed S0 can be cheaply recomputed with changed exchange or resolved supply capacity.
The contract uses generic dt/[t0,t1], not day or calendar boundaries.
No fixed coupling-window duration is assumed.
Final capacity-respecting mass closure is explicitly reserved for transactional runtime composition.
D3 does not alter the SWAP-MODFLOW head/flux interface; lateral exchange remains signed physical mass.
Mass conservation is hard: the legacy -0.1 cm dry-floor gap is explicitly not admitted as physical tolerance.
D3 consumes physical exchange results; it does not hide or regularize D2 sensitivities.
No extra full SWAP runs are introduced by the algebraic limiter.
Limiter cost and state are O(1) per column plus per-level scaling only when active.
No MODFLOW cell fraction or tile topology appears in the limiter.
Deep-vadose transfer remains external and unrelated.
All cross-component mass terms are explicit; no stored water may disappear during composition.
Limiter arithmetic is independent of the chosen soil-water solver implementation.
Qualified D2 exchange and existing drainage physics are reused rather than duplicated.
No HeadCalc internals are referenced.
Supply availability is physical control input; mass closure is not a solver-performance policy.
Limiter work is bounded and deterministic; invalid capacity closure fails/retries rather than iterating without bound.
Frozen proportional limiter semantics remain characterized while source mass gaps are explicitly held, not silently normalized.
Limiter-active, alpha, capacity use, required actual supply and mass residual are runtime-diagnostic quantities.
No optional persistent state is allocated by D3.
Control components resolve supply enablement and runtime owns final system composition/ledger.
No midnight, daily, legacy-file or direct MODFLOW assumptions are introduced.
D3 readiness and each mass-source risk are explicitly checked against all invariants.

mass_source_holds: D3-RISK-01 raw WSCAP cannot stand in for resolved available supply on all control routes.
D3-RISK-02 the legacy dry-floor -0.1 cm window cannot authorize unmatched water creation/destruction.
D3-RISK-03 actual q_supply must be materialized as a first-class physical result.
D3-RISK-04 limiter-active mixed-sign per-level scaling is held from the initial production route.
D3-RISK-05 pre-solver availability limiting cannot certify final storage before QRapDra and top-surface exchange are known.
D3-RISK-06 a dry-floor state requiring supply above capacity is not an acceptable trial.
D3-RISK-07 limiter and runtime must not double-book the same physical transfer.
scope_holds: No production candidate is admitted by D3 readiness.
Fixed-weir and automatic-weir evolution remain D4/D5.
Atomic commit/rollback and accepted-ledger implementation remain D6.
